result:
The frozen DG1 candidate (`sha256:7fcc4943…b39367`, commit `85e5bbd`) **fails** QA verification: two High problems would block a release, alongside one Medium and four Low findings.

I confirmed the candidate ID in the repository and in a separate disposable clone. The commit at the current HEAD only adds review metadata, which is allowed. I read no other reviewer's record before deciding.

**What passed on the candidate:**
- **Build and static checks:** the offline install from the committed lockfile downloaded nothing and left it unchanged. Typecheck, build, lint, formatting, the API contract check (33 operations), the no-CDN check and the colour-contrast check all passed.
- **Unit tests:** 130 of 130 passed.
- **Database:** migrations apply to a fresh PostgreSQL database, and the audit table rejects UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE, even for the owner.
- **Acceptance suites:** A12 (cross-scope access denied, 14 tests), A13 (job idempotency, 5) and A14 (optimistic concurrency, 5) all passed.
- **Browser tests:** 20 of 20 passed in English and Arabic on the real stack, with no accessibility violations. A20 passed: Arabic right-to-left is the default and the English switch persists. A changed design token also shows up in the rendered page.
- **New spec of my own** (6 of 6 passed):
  - The branding API returns exactly the seven tokens marked provisional, and 401 when signed out.
  - No requests go to outside hosts; the fonts are served from the app itself.
  - The header shows a text wordmark with a provisional badge, and no page claims official Mobily or PMI status.
- **Clean start (A18):** passed from a fresh checkout. Stopping the background worker leaves the API working.
- **Other checks:** the module-boundary check catches imports I injected to break it. Every CI job depends on the delivery-gates job. The sandboxed installer tests pass 7 of 7 when given a writable package store. The validator passes, and all 12 DG1 requirements are marked done with existing evidence files.

**Findings** (written to `docs/delivery/reviews/DG1/round-1/qa-verifier.findings.json`):

| ID | Severity | Requirement | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-DG1-201 | **High** (mandatory) | REQ-S19-006 | The integration test suite fails on two fresh databases. The new branding-tokens operation was never added to the contract tests (it was left for "the reviewers"), so the CI integration job would fail. The endpoint itself returns the right data. |
| F-DG1-202 | **High** (mandatory) | REQ-DLV-033 | The production build can't start the API. The script that assembles the runtime (the same one the Docker image uses) leaves out the design-tokens package, so the API crashes on startup. My own A18 test runs from the development build, so it didn't catch this. |
| F-DG1-203 | Medium | REQ-DLV-033 | Container images are not pinned to exact versions (10 problems), so the CI images job always fails. |
| F-DG1-204 | Low | REQ-DLV-033 | The software bill of materials records an out-of-date lockfile fingerprint; the package list itself is correct. |
| F-DG1-205 | Low | REQ-DLV-025 | The copy of the CI workflow under `docs/architecture/ci/` no longer matches the installed one. |
| F-DG1-206 | Low | REQ-DLV-042 | The installer tests' "must not happen" cases still pass when every install fails, so they can pass without proving anything. |
| F-DG1-207 | Low | REQ-S19-006, REQ-S16-003 | The register cites 32 operations and "8/8 contract tests", which is out of date. REQ-S16-003 still promises "six modules with test suites", but under decision D-047 only some are built now. I judge that acceptable for DG1, but the register text should be updated. |

**Your open items:**
- **Module scope (D-047):** acceptable for DG1, subject to the register update in F-DG1-207.
- **Status codes and sign-in check:** acceptable for P1. The API returns 400/403 where the contract has no 422. The web app tests whether dev sign-in exists by sending an empty dev-login request, and the contract allows both answers. It no longer calls `/auth/options`.
- **Two-browser race:** acceptable with the single-worker setting in CI.
- **`.env.example` location:** not a DG1 issue.

**Could not be checked:**
- The Docker/Compose clean start, because access to the Docker daemon was denied.
- A live CI run.
- Whether the installer's network is limited to the package registry, because the sandbox has no network.
- `pnpm deps:verify`, which needs the registry; it wasn't required.

**Corrections to my own test scripts:**
- My new spec's first run wrongly flagged the product's own Arabic disclaimer ("not certified by PMI") as a claim. I fixed the patterns and checked them against sample sentences.
- My worker-stop script's first outbox check used a badly built database address; I fixed it and reran. Both runs' logs are in the evidence.

**Cleanup:** I removed the disposable clone, the package store copy and the database work directory, and no test processes remain. A few small scratch files are left in the run's private temporary directory, which the runner deletes when the run ends.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG1/round-1/` and `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/qa/round-1/`:
- qa-verifier.json
- qa-verifier.md
- qa-verifier.findings.json

The new spec is at `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/qa/tests/dg1-r1-branding-fonts-wordmark.spec.ts`.
